title: Declare the tk commands the factory depends on, and guard them
description:
THE DELIVERABLE THAT OUTLIVES THIS EPIC. Once the factory reaches ticks through the CLI, that CLI is a contract — and an undeclared contract is one ticks breaks by accident on a quiet Tuesday.

PRECEDENT TO COPY: cloud/sandbox/required-tk-commands already does exactly this for the container, and the image's last Dockerfile layer install-checks every listed command against the tk it just built. Follow that shape rather than inventing a new one; ideally the two lists converge or one references the other.

The list must name the commands AND the flags relied on — 'tk show <id> --json' and 'tk list --json' at minimum, whatever else tick 7o5 ends up using, and the sandbox's existing entries.

THE TEST IS THE POINT. Add a test that FAILS when a listed command or flag is removed or renamed. A list nobody checks is a comment. Decide how to assert it — invoking the built binary is the strongest signal and matches what the Dockerfile does; reading the cobra command tree is faster but proves less. Say which you chose and what it does not catch.

Out of scope: JSON SHAPE stability (a field being renamed inside --json output). That is Phase 2's contract artifact, not this list. Note the boundary in the file so nobody assumes this test covers more than it does.
acceptance_criteria: A committed list names every tk command and flag the factory relies on. A test fails when any listed command or flag is removed or renamed — demonstrated by removing one on purpose and showing the failure. The list's relationship to cloud/sandbox/required-tk-commands is stated. The file says explicitly that JSON field stability is NOT covered here. go test ./... green.
